findings.text: — §5's done-when states the test "reports the number of citations it checked, which equals the number of `reckon <verb>` occurrences an independent `grep -oE` over the same corpus finds at that head"; but a raw `grep -oE 'reckon [a-z][a-z-]*'` over §5's own corpus (skills/**/*.md, PLAN-FORMAT.md, the repo `AGENTS.md` files, reckon/crew/prompts/*.md) returns 327 occurrences and includes clear non-citations — e.g. `reckon itself` (AGENTS.md:184), `reckon resolves` (coordinator-reference.md:506), `reckon did` (:525), `reckon can` (worker-backends.md:28), `reckon skills` (reckon-sync/SKILL.md:109), `reckon prepares` (worker-backends.md:34) — while the source extractor counted only 261 command invocations by restricting to backtick spans, fenced lines and line-initial commands; so the equality is unattainable unless the grep is scoped exactly like the extractor, at which point it is no longer the "independent" control the done-when relies on and the plan names no grep pattern to scope it. WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: this is the node's gating measure, so as written the worker either fails the gate or quietly constrains the "independent" grep until it agrees, which is the fail-open control the section exists to avoid; it is the residual of the earlier done_when-1 finding after its `grep -c`→`grep -oE` edit, which fixed lines-vs-citations but left occurrences-vs-citations.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves: `PLAN-FORMAT.md:321/:330`, `sprint-orchestration.md:1011`, `coordinator-reference.md:593-614`, `SKILL.md:185-211`, the health-skill-drift report path, and commit `807053fb6`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's positive control compares the test's command-citation count against an independent `grep -oE` occurrence count of `reckon <verb>` over the same corpus, but that grep counts non-citation prose occurrences too, so the two figures cannot reconcile as written.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the test sits at `tests/test_cited_commands_exist.py`, the two control figures go into the run manifest, and the source report is cited at a durable path under `~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new artefact is mechanism-named (`test_cited_commands_exist.py`, "every command a skill or format document cites exists"); no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, and no changelog prose is introduced.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause matches the cited evidence (the report confirms nothing fails on a renamed command and the three dead citations were found by reading), the mechanism (a corpus scan comparing verb chains and flags to each command's `--help`) can produce the done-when, and the mechanism runs on a real path (a committed pytest under `tests/`, collected by the suite with no new production caller needed).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 delivers one thing (a test asserting every cited `reckon` command exists, plus the repairs that make it pass); the test, the `PLAN-FORMAT.md` repair and the table replacement are facets of that one deliverable, not two deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5 declares its ordering against §3 in prose ("This section runs after §3, which rewrites `SKILL.md` and the same references directory…"), resolving the earlier wiring-1 finding; the two evidence gates it sits beside gate s3 correctly and no relationship points at the wrong node.
